summary: Sticky residency refresh delay causing intermittent p50 jitter and cross-region fallback
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports brief increases in p50 latency (50-120ms above baseline) across eu-west for requests pinned to EU residency. The spike correlates with background residency-refresh events and at times results in a short fallback to a US egress path for a subset of requests.

Impact:
- Intermittent p50 latency increases seen by NovusHealth web app users in EU region during business hours.
- No customer-observed 5xxs or lost responses; errors are not reported.
- Affects SLA-sensitive flows that must remain EU-e2e due to data residency constraints.

Environment:
- Tenant: novus-prod (enterprise/private deployment using Redwood Private control plane)
- Region: eu-west primary, failover to us-east seen in traces
- Models: redwood-v1-medium production pin
- Time window: recurring ~every 10-18 minutes for short bursts (30-120s).

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send 50-100 small-chat requests pinned to EU residency over 5 minutes from NovusHealth frontend.
2) Observe p50 and trace egress path.
3) At ~10-18 minute cadence some requests show 150-220ms added latency and traces indicate egress hop to us-east for ~30-90s.

Observed behavior:
- Traces show control-plane residency-refresh job runs and a small fraction of tokens pick a route that resolves to a US edge before the pin refresh fully completes.
- Client-side retried requests are fine but initial p50 moves up.

Expected behavior:
- Pin refresh should be atomic for an active token or should prefer sticky existing egress until refresh window closes. No cross-region egress should be observed for enterprise tenants with strict residency.

Logs/links:
- Sample trace: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/novus/trace-20260310-1223
- Control plane job run logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/app/control-plane/2026-03-10-refresh
comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 - Maya Chen (Support): Opened ticket after receiving customer report. Asked for request IDs and example traces; provided initial guidance to increase local client retry window.

2026-03-10 09:42 - NovusHealth (Customer): Provided several trace IDs and noted spikes correspond to internal token refresh cycles. Customer is concerned about EU egress during bursts due to compliance reviews.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Arjun Patel (SRE): Acknowledged receipt, escalated to control-plane owner, and requested control-plane job schedule and TTLs. Assigned investigation to residency routing subteam.

2026-03-11 14:30 - Control-plane Owner (Elena Ruiz): Observed that residency-lock-refresh job has a staggered worker window by AZ to avoid thundering herd; a small timing gap can leave routing table entries inconsistent for ~30-90s. Reproduced a quick replay that triggered US fallback for ~0.7% of requests during stagger window.

2026-03-12 08:20 - Arjun Patel (SRE): Noted mitigation steps: reduce stagger window for enterprise tenants that have strict residency flag, and add a sticky egress preference during refresh. Drafted PR to gate behavior by tenant flag.

2026-03-13 11:05 - NovusHealth (Customer): Customer accepted temporary mitigation if we limit any cross-region egress to under 0.01% and will await permanent fix. Asked for ETA on permanent fix and whether this needs a contractual change.

2026-03-13 16:00 - Maya Chen (Support): Updated customer that a temporary config change is scheduled and a permanent code fix is targeted in next sprint; asked customer to confirm acceptable maintenance window.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Collected traces and control-plane job schedules. Identified correlation between residency-lock-refresh and p50 spikes.

2026-03-11: Replayed refresh job in staging. Confirmed staggered refresh can leave partial routing entries where edge selection falls back to default egress resolver (which in our setup can be US edge for some DNS answers).
2026-03-11: Rate of affected requests ~0.5-1% during window on replay for tenant with normal TTL; effect increases if client side pre-resolve behavior is present.

2026-03-12: Root cause hypothesis: control-plane worker stagger combined with DNS cache TTL and edge ip rotation causes a small race where egress resolution prefers a non-EU edge until the new residency stamp propagates to the routing layer.

2026-03-12: Temporary mitigation approach: set a 'refresh-sticky' flag for enterprise tenants so that in-flight tokens continue to honor previous routing entries until refresh completes, and reduce stagger window to 10s for tenants with strict residency.
2026-03-12: Code PR reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/412 (adds tenant-level refresh-sticky flag and configuration toggle)
2026-03-13: Verified in staging with NovusHealth-like footprint: p50 jitter eliminated in 5 test runs; fallback rate reduced to <0.01%.
2026-03-13: Risk assessment: low risk to broader fleet if gated by tenant flag; requires config push to Private control plane for Novus tenant.
2026-03-13: Linked INT ticket for Ops to perform config push: INT-2243.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-13: Temporary mitigation scheduled: set refresh-sticky=true and reduce worker stagger to 10s for novus-prod during maintenance window 2026-03-14 02:00-03:00 UTC. This is a config-only change for Private control plane.
2026-03-13: Customer notified and accepted maintenance window. Post-change verification plan includes 1 hour of synthetic traffic and sampling traces every 5 minutes.
Planned permanent fix: make refresh-sticky default for tenants with data-residency policy and add an atomic refresh propagation mechanism (tracked in backlog, target: next sprint).

Follow-ups: Update runbook for residency refresh (confluence link), add monitoring alert for cross-region egress rate for enterprise tenants, and include mention in Customer Release Notes for NovusHealth.
Status: Mitigation approved and queued; permanent fix scheduled.
